_description: Phase 3 comparison-page backlog. Only pairs with real confusion or decision-relevance are listed - see calculator-architecture.md / seo-architecture.md for pairs explicitly considered and rejected (MRR vs ARR, Retention vs Churn, NRR vs GRR - all already one page).

comparisons.why: Both answer 'was this spend worth it', with different denominators (spend vs. cost) that regularly get conflated.
CAC counts paying customers, CPA counts any defined conversion - the two get used interchangeably in casual usage.
Different bidding models (per-click vs. per-1000-impressions); a buyer choosing between them is genuine decision intent.
Both are click ratios with different denominators (impressions/delivered vs. opens) - a common email-marketing confusion point.
Three margin calculators with increasingly broad cost bases; one three-way comparison page serves this better than pairwise ones.
ARPU is a per-period snapshot, LTV projects across a customer's lifetime - frequently confused when sizing a business.
A CI calculator can be (mis)used to eyeball significance; the two answer related but distinct questions.
Same equation, solved for the opposite variable - users often aren't sure which one they actually need.
Same formula shape, different spend/customer population - a frequent methodology mix-up in CAC reporting.
Customer-count churn vs. dollar-weighted churn (an NRR output) can move in opposite directions in the same period.
Both are single-number SaaS health checks; teams often want to know which one to report.
Mobile 'activation' is a specific product event, not a generic funnel conversion - worth a direct contrast.
Cost to install vs. cost to acquire a paying customer - a common mobile-UA budgeting confusion.
